# vela3.1-pico-150m

The smallest Vela 3.1 model, a 150M encoder for small CPU hosts, with the same questions and spans as vela3.1-pico-380m. Opt-in; it has no calibrated thresholds yet.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Repository | [`vllm-sr/vela3.1-pico-150m`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/vela3.1-pico-150m), pinned at `dad77ad7a83c` |
| Family | [Vela 3.1](model-runtime/supported-models/vela-3/overview.md) |
| Parameters | 0.153B loaded |
| Backbone | UltraBERT |
| Precision (`--dtype auto`) | FP32 on every device |
| Weights | about 0.6 GB at FP32 |
| Device memory | 2 GiB or more |
| Reads | text |

## Question types

| Type | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `choice` | Yes |
| `noul` | Yes |
| `score` | No |
| `set` | Yes, asked as one `noul` per label |
| `span` | Yes, on the `router` span head |

## Built-in questions

The Vela 3.1 family was trained on the Router's built-in
questions, so the Router asks each one in its trained form; the
[support matrix](system-one/reference/support-matrix.md) lists which.

:::note
This model has no calibrated thresholds: a built-in question without a
`predicate` uses 0.5, and the configuration load warns with
`uncalibrated_preset`.
:::

## Hardware

Each time it loads, the model compares its answers with the reference
answers recorded for its revision. They are recorded for:

- CPU (`cpu`)

On an AMD GPU or an NVIDIA GPU no reference is recorded, so the model serves
there with its self-check reported as `unverified`.

[Choose a model](model-runtime/get-started/choose-a-model.md#hardware) lists the
validated hardware.

## Quantization

The runtime loads no quantized packages of the Vela 3.1 family:
it runs at its published precision.

## Deploy it

Serve it on its own in Engine mode, to ask it directly:

<Tabs groupId="platform">
<TabItem value="cpu" label="CPU" default>

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/vela3.1-pico-150m --engine --platform cpu
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="rocm" label="AMD GPU">

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/vela3.1-pico-150m --engine --platform rocm
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="cuda" label="NVIDIA GPU">

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/vela3.1-pico-150m --engine --platform cuda
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Or make it the Router's decision model:

```yaml title="config.yaml"
global:
  model_catalog:
    deployments:
      primary:
        provider: model_runtime
        artifact: vllm-sr/vela3.1-pico-150m
        device: auto
    system:
      decision_model: {deployment: primary}
```

`device: auto` takes the first validated GPU with enough free memory, else
the CPU; name `rocm:0` or `cuda:0` to pin a GPU.

To run it on another host and attach the Router to it:

```bash
vllm-srun serve vllm-sr/vela3.1-pico-150m --device auto --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8100
```

Then set `endpoint: http://<host>:8100` and
`model: vela3.1-pico-150m` on the deployment; see
[Attach to a runtime you run](model-runtime/deploy/connect-the-router.md#attach-to-a-runtime-you-run).
